key_insight: Combining plasma DNA fragmentomics with glycoprotein biomarkers detected malignant pancreatic cystic neoplasms better than either approach alone.
clinical_relevance: This investigational diagnostic approach could help refine selection for endoscopic ultrasound, but it is not a drug discovery study or an established clinical test.
method: Performed whole-genome sequencing of pretreatment plasma DNA from 341 participants.
Trained and validated a fragmentomics machine-learning model using 121 pancreatic cancer cases and 121 matched healthy controls.
Independently evaluated 99 patients with pancreatic cysts referred for endoscopic ultrasound, including combinations with CA19-9, CA125 and CEA.
evidence_signal: Among 99 cyst patients, 11 had malignancy during 24.6 months of follow-up; combined biomarkers achieved AUROC 0.92 versus 0.67 for fragmentomics alone, with 91% sensitivity and 88% specificity.
watch_item: Only 11 malignant cyst cases were evaluated in an endoscopic-ultrasound referral cohort, so broader prospective validation is needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Plasma DNA fragmentomic analysis for evaluation of patients with pancreatic cystic neoplasms
